message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most famous American composers across different eras and styles:

| Era / Style | Composer | Notable Works |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| **Early Colonial & Revolutionary** | William Billings (1746–1800) | *"New England Psalmist"* |
| **19th‑Century Romantic** | Stephen Foster (1826–1864) | “Oh! Susanna,” “Camptown Races” |
| **Late 19th‑Early 20th Century** | Edward MacDowell (1857–1908) | *“Woodland Sketches”* |
| **Early 20th Century (American Classical)** | Charles Ives (1874–1954) | *“The Unanswered Question”*, *“Concord Hymn”* |
| **Mid‑20th Century (Modernist/Neoclassical)** | Aaron Copland (1900–1990) | *“Appalachian Spring,” “Rodeo”* |
| **Jazz & Popular Music** | Duke Ellington (1899–1974) | *“Mood Indigo,” “Take the A Train”* |
| **Broadway & Musical Theatre** | Richard Rodgers (1902–1979) | *“Oklahoma!”*, *“Carousel”* |
| **Film Scores** | Bernard Herrmann (1911–1975) | *“Psycho,” “Vertigo”* |
| **Contemporary Classical** | Philip Glass (born 1937) | *“Glassworks,” “Einstein on the Beach”* |
| **Film & Television** | John Williams (born 1942) | *“Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones”* |
| **Contemporary Pop & Rock** | Hans Zimmer (born 1957) | *“Inception,” “Interstellar”* |

These composers have had a profound impact on both American and global music culture, spanning genres from classical to jazz, Broadway, film scores, and beyond.
